_START_HERE: You are continuing the Pattom signal-timing and low-emission intersection project. Step 1: read AI_RULES.md, then HANDOFF.md (sections 2 and 18) and handoff_addendum_2026-10-14.md, then PRD.md (section 8.1 is the source register: input values come only from there or from the footage), ARCHITECTURE.md, PLAN.md, IRC_SP41_extract.md, EMISSION_SOURCES.md and this file. Step 2: continue the first task in review_order whose status is IN_PROGRESS and which is not marked ongoing; if none, take the first task whose status is PENDING, whose T dependencies are all DONE and whose O dependencies are all DECIDED. Ids starting with T are tasks (see the 'tasks' section). Ids starting with O are open decisions (see 'open_decisions'). Step 3: do the task, produce the output named in 'output', then check it against 'done_when'. Step 4: set the status, fill 'evidence' with what was produced (file, table, or number with its source), add a line to the task's history and to _meta.history. Step 5: never mark DONE without evidence. Status rule: BLOCKED means the task waits on an open decision that is not yet DECIDED. A task waiting only on other tasks stays PENDING. When an open decision becomes DECIDED, set the tasks that waited only on it back to PENDING. If a task needs an open decision, stop and ask the user instead of choosing. If the guide has not answered, the user may close an item as 'decided, guide pending' with a date; record that in the decision's guide_confirmed field and keep it visible.

_meta.project: Optimization of Traffic Management Strategies for Vehicular Emission Reduction at Urban Intersections (Pattom, Thiruvananthapuram)
working_rules: AI_RULES.md applies at all times. HANDOFF.md section 2 (hard constraints) always applies.
Never invent traffic counts, emission factors, capacity values, CI weights, MCE scores, signal timings or SUMO results. Every number needs a source, a measurement or a stated assumption.
Label every value as measured, derived or estimated. Keep these separate in all tables.

Do not write code unless the user asks for it in that session (user instruction, 14 Oct 2026: planning phase). Do not write files during a discussion unless asked; after a planning discussion, ask once whether to update the ledger.
Only the MCE-selected alternative is simulated in SUMO, together with the existing case.
Alternatives are developed before the MCE. SUMO results are not used to score the MCE.
The redesign scope is signal timing: existing fixed timing compared with dynamic (traffic-responsive) timing. No widening, new lanes or reconstruction.
Do not claim dynamic timing reduces emissions before the data show it. It is a hypothesis.
A task is DONE only when its done_when condition is met and evidence is recorded.
Resetting a task to PENDING never deletes history.
Status rule: BLOCKED only while a dependency O id is not DECIDED. Otherwise PENDING.

Input values come only from the footage or the source register (PRD section 8.1, D15). A value the register lacks is a gap: report it, propose sources, and let the user decide. Do not fill it from memory or another source.

D2.text: The redesign scope is signal timing and phasing: the existing fixed timing is compared with re-optimised and traffic-responsive alternatives, within the existing geometry. If the data show problems that timing cannot address, report them as findings and future work.

D3.text: MCE uses the five PPT criteria: congestion reduction, emission reduction, safety improvement, construction cost, land requirement.

D6.text: Two recording slots of about 1.5 hours each: off-peak and peak. The evening outflow (from about 4:15 pm) is the main peak. Video is the ground truth; validation is by manual counting of playback clips.

D11.text: Capacity comes from IRC SP 41 (1994), supplied by the guide. Signalised approach capacity uses section 7.6: capacity = g x s / c, with s = 525 w PCU/h for approach widths of 5.5 to 18 m. The PCU table (Table 3.1 or Table III-1) is still to be chosen.

T24.title: Choose the emission-factor source and method
T24.output: Named source, pollutant list, vehicle categories, units and handling of unknown fleet details
T24.done_when: Source cited and unit consistency checked against the activity basis
T24.evidence: Sources read so far: India GHG Program road-transport technical paper (CO2 only, per km); IISc ENVIS table from ARAI 2007, read from the user's screenshot (CO2, CH4, N2O per km, no three-wheeler row, values not independently verified). Not yet read: IIASA India road-emissions work and an Emerald paper on MOVES idling (web fetch blocked by bot protection, so the user is to open and upload the PDFs); a Delhi idling study; Napier page redirected to a holding page. No source found so far covers CO, NOx and PM with an idle- or speed-based method. Research run 14 Oct 2026 (EMISSION_SOURCES.md): ARAI 2007 Table I gives g/km for CO, HC, NOx, CO2, PM by class; idle g/min exists only in ARAI Annexure IV (not public); CSIR-CRRI idle fuel rates exist (motorcycle 0.14, three-wheeler 0.24, car 0.6, bus 0.9 L/h, reported); IVE is a free VSP-bin model applied in Pune and Chennai. No open Indian idle CO/HC/NOx/PM rates or three-wheeler NOx/PM by speed were found. One citation checked by hand (Sharma et al. 2019, J. Cleaner Production 212:8-21); the rest are as reported.
T24.notes: The AI researches and proposes; the user and guide confirm, which closes O5 (D13). The method must respond to signal timing. YOLO cannot identify fuel type, model year or emission standard; state this assumption. Also look for a source with g/km factors for CO, NOx and PM by vehicle type, including three-wheelers (the primary ARAI report behind the ENVIS table may have them; not verified). A per-km, driving-cycle source does not respond to timing on its own; a speed or idle based method is needed on top. Interim proposal: CO2-first (idle time x idle fuel rate x fuel carbon factor, plus ARAI g/km for moving vehicles), then add CO, HC, NOx, PM when the papers are obtained (T49). Fuel type is assumed per class because video cannot tell it. Sources are registered per D15 (EMISSION_SOURCES.md section 2); each is marked verified or reported.

T28.title: Define how congestion and emission reduction are scored before SUMO
T28.output: Written scoring method for the two reduction criteria
T28.done_when: Method approved by the guide (part of closing O13)
T28.notes: Analytical estimate from observed flows (D8). SUMO results cannot be used here because only the winner is simulated afterwards. The method must be valid for each alternative type: a Webster-type delay formula assumes fixed-time, isolated and undersaturated (volume/capacity below 1) operation, so state what is used when volume/capacity reaches or exceeds 1 and how actuated or adaptive control is approximated. If the method cannot score an alternative, say so and either drop it or record the limit. IRC SP 41 sections 7.6.3 and 7.6.4 give the fixed-time cycle-time and green-split formulas (Co = (1.5 L + 5)/(1 - Y); g1/g2 = y1/y2), usable for a re-optimised fixed plan. They give no delay formula and nothing on actuated or adaptive control, so another source is needed. Do not quote the 120 s sentence (p. 78) or the right-turn formula (p. 77) before checking IRC 93; both look misprinted. GAP under D15: no registered source gives a delay formula for the pre-SUMO estimate. Before T28 closes, the user decides which source to add; candidates with citations are proposed in that session.
